events.title: CVE-2026-98432 — In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period tcp_v4_syn_
events.summary: A serious Linux kernel IPv4 TCP race condition has been documented: request-socket options can be read by one CPU while another CPU is freeing them after an RCU grace period during retransmitted SYN handling. The record lists CVE-2026-98432 with a CVSS score of 9.8 and CVE-2026-84295 with a CVSS score of 10.0, and headlines say the flaw can enable remote root on major distributions.
events.why_it_matters: With critical severity and CVSS scores of 9.8 and 10.0, this Linux kernel flaw poses a serious risk to affected servers, especially given headlines saying it enables remote root and impacts distributions such as Ubuntu and Red Hat. Defenders should track vendor kernel updates and prioritise patching internet-facing systems. The record does not indicate KEV listing or exploitation in the wild.
